title: Microsoft Teams: Facilitator Protection skill warns of suspected social engineering
notes: claim 44: severity blocker on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Hold: the PowerShell reference describes the printed call as unblocking an app, so it does not establish a safe blocking command. The briefing also treats published Facilitator prerequisites as unconfirmed and turns conditional warnings into a compulsory choice in its impact rationale.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Facilitator can be allowed or blocked through Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Facilitator > Allow or Block.
claims.quote:
In the left rail navigation, select Teams apps > Manage apps.
In the apps list's search box, search for Facilitator.
Select Facilitator from the app list.
In the actions menu, select Allow or Block.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <FacilitatorAppId> -IsBlocked $true is the automation equivalent of blocking Facilitator.
claims.quote:
Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true
Unblocks Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b).
claims.fix: Remove the runnable blocking call and set controls[0].api to null. Add to its note: 'The Update-M365TeamsApp reference describes its -IsBlocked $true example as unblocking an app; a reliable blocking call is not established by that reference.' Keep the verified admin UI path.

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: The only documented Facilitator control is the app's Allow or Block action.
claims.quote:
You can also use app centric management to allow and block, create policies, and assign users.

claims.fix: Replace 'The only documented control is the Facilitator app’s Allow or Block action, which governs Facilitator as a whole' with 'The table lists the Facilitator app’s Allow or Block action, which governs Facilitator as a whole.' Do not imply that other Facilitator controls are undocumented.

claims.where: rationale: impact
claims.claim: Users in Facilitator meetings with outsiders will see warnings and must choose to end the meeting or restrict information sharing.
claims.quote: If a suspected attempt is detected, users will receive a warning.- Users will have options to end the meeting or temporarily restrict information sharing.
claims.fix: Replace the impact rationale with: 'Medium. Users in Facilitator meetings with outside participants may see a warning if a suspected attempt is detected, with options to end the meeting or temporarily restrict information sharing.'
